intro: A nearest-neighbor system needs a query-by-candidate distance table. Its orientation determines which axis can be ranked.
task: Return squared Euclidean distances between every row of X and every row of Y.
requirements: X and Y are nonempty finite matrices with the same positive number of features.
Return a NumPy array of shape (len(X), len(Y)); do not take square roots.
Identical rows have zero distance; feature order must agree in both inputs.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: X[:, None, :] and Y[None, :, :] align rows while retaining the feature axis.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Reduce axis=-1, not either observation axis.

explanation: Broadcasting a query axis against a candidate axis exposes all pairwise differences. Summing only the feature axis leaves the required query-by-candidate table.
Squared distance preserves nearest-neighbor ordering and avoids a square root. Its numeric values are not ordinary Euclidean distances, so a distance threshold must use matching units.
Translate both matrices by the same vector and compare results. Then translate only one. Use that experiment to explain why shared preprocessing matters.
